xwhatsapp-strokecopylinkgoogleAdd Al Jazeera on GoogleinfoThe funeral of Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf and his family [Mahmoud Issa/Reuters]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 25 Nov 202625 Nov 2026Israeli attacks on Gaza have killed at least seven Palestinians, including a senior security official, according to medical sources and local officials.

In a statement on Wednesday, Gaza’s Interior Ministry said Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, was killed in an attack on Shati refugee camp. Al-Awf’s wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15, were also killed, it added.

The ministry described the killings as a “horrific massacre perpetrated by the Israeli occupation forces when they bombed [the family’s] residence in the Shati refugee camp” in Gaza City.

The attack is part of “ongoing attempts to undermine the security apparatus in the Gaza Strip in an effort to spread chaos within Palestinian society”, it added.

A source at al-Shifa Hospital confirmed to Al Jazeera that four people from the same family were killed and several were wounded in an Israeli attack on an apartment in the refugee camp.

The attack came less than 24 hours after the killing of the Internal Security Service’s director general, Brigadier-General Naim Abu Nahal.

In another deadly incident, two Palestinians were killed in a drone attack on the al-Karama neighbourhood in Gaza City while a seventh Palestinian man was killed when an Israeli attack hit a tent sheltering displaced people in Jabalia al-Balad in northern Gaza.

Medical sources at the Nasser Medical Complex reported that a Palestinian girl was injured when she was shot by Israeli forces in areas outside their control in Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

Near-daily Israeli violations of a “ceasefire” in Gaza have been recorded since it began in October 2025. Israeli air attacks regularly hit the enclave, and at least 1,680 people have been killed during the “ceasefire” and more than 6,000 injured as Israel’s genocidal war continues.

Hamas called on the guarantor states of the “ceasefire” to intervene immediately “to rein in the occupation, impose a halt to its crimes and obligate it to adhere to the agreement’s path”.
